title: 275 - Super Mario Bros. 3
method: claude-code: written from the transcript, links verified by script

items.name: Super Mario Bros. 3
items.description: The episode's game: the 1988 Nintendo platformer with world maps, power-ups like the raccoon suit, and 90 levels.

items.name: Super Mario Bros.
items.description: The first NES Mario game, already voted onto the Essential Games List and compared throughout.

items.name: Color a Dinosaur
items.description: An earlier NES game the show has talked about so much it is a running in-joke.

items.name: Super Mario All-Stars
items.description: The SNES collection of remade NES Mario games, joked about as a future episode.

items.name: Super Nintendo Entertainment System
items.description: Nintendo's 16-bit console, launched in North America in 1991 after the NES era.

items.name: Super Mario World
items.description: The SNES follow-up with Yoshi and the cape, constantly compared with Super Mario Bros. 3.

items.name: New Super Mario Bros.
items.description: The modern side-scrolling Mario series that follows the Super Mario Bros. 3 format.

items.name: Shigeru Miyamoto
items.description: The Nintendo designer behind Mario, credited for plussing up the first game.

items.name: Super Mario Bros. 2
items.description: The NES sequel the show counts as Super Mario Bros. 2, built from a different game and not by Miyamoto's main team.

items.name: Mario Is Missing!
items.description: An upcoming educational Mario game on the NES the hosts are unsure about.

items.name: Mario's Time Machine
items.description: An upcoming educational Mario game on the NES the hosts are unsure about.

items.name: Yoshi
items.description: The dinosaur companion introduced in Super Mario World, mentioned as a reason one host prefers that game.

items.name: Koopalings
items.description: The seven Koopa kids who guard each world's airship, later retconned as Bowser's cousins.

items.name: Hammer Bros.
items.description: Wandering map enemies that feel like bigger boss fights than Boom Boom.

links.label: Wikipedia: List of Mario franchise enemies

items.name: Super Mario Sunshine
items.description: GameCube Mario game blamed for changing Bowser's backstory and the Koopalings' relationship to him.

items.name: The Legend of Kage
items.description: An earlier NES game used as an example of a stale gameplay loop.

items.name: The Tower of Druaga
items.description: Namco game invoked as a comparison for a game where failing a mini-game blocks progress; covered on the show's Bites feed.

items.name: Sonic Adventure
items.description: Used as an example of 3D Sonic games that grade you at the end of each level.

items.name: Devil May Cry
items.description: Series suggested as a better comparison for style-based scoring at the end of levels.

items.name: Boo
items.description: The ghost enemy introduced in Super Mario Bros. 3 that only chases you when you look away.

links.label: Wikipedia: List of Mario franchise enemies

items.name: Super Mario 3D World
items.description: The game with the cat suit, mentioned as a modern Mario power-up.

items.name: Super Mario Maker
items.description: Level-building Mario game, the only modern 2D Mario one host has played.

items.name: Final Fantasy Pixel Remaster
items.description: Remastered re-releases of the early Final Fantasy games cited in the remake discussion.

links.label: Wikipedia: Final Fantasy Pixel Remaster
links.note: Series of Final Fantasy video game remasters

items.name: Dragon Quest III
items.description: The RPG getting a modern remake in an Octopath Traveler style, used in the remaster discussion.

items.name: Game Boy Advance
items.description: Nintendo handheld that got Super Mario Advance 4: Super Mario Bros. 3.

items.name: Super Mario Advance 4: Super Mario Bros. 3
items.description: The Game Boy Advance remake with e-Reader levels, released with new content.

links.label: Wikipedia: Super Mario Advance 4: Super Mario Bros. 3

items.name: Nintendo e-Reader
items.description: Game Boy Advance card scanner used to unlock extra levels and power-ups.

links.label: Wikipedia: Nintendo e-Reader
links.note: Add-on for the Game Boy Advance

items.name: Wii U
items.description: Console whose Virtual Console release included the e-Reader levels, no longer sold.

links.label: Wikipedia: Wii U
links.note: Home video game console by Nintendo

items.name: The Wizard
items.description: The 1989 film that doubled as a trailer for Super Mario Bros. 3.

items.name: The Adventures of Super Mario Bros. 3
items.description: The 1990 animated TV series based on the game, with Bowser called Koopa.

links.label: Wikipedia: The Adventures of Super Mario Bros. 3

items.name: The Super Mario Bros. Super Show!
items.description: The earlier half live-action, half-cartoon Mario show.

links.label: Wikipedia: The Super Mario Bros. Super Show!

items.name: Super Mario Bros. (film)
items.description: The 1993 live-action movie the hosts compare to the live-action segments of the Super Show.

links.label: Wikipedia: Super Mario Bros. (film)
links.note: 1993 film by Rocky Morton and Annabel Jankel

items.name: Super Smash Bros. Melee
items.description: Where one host learned Bowser is called Koopa in Japanese by switching languages.

items.name: King Koopa's Kool Kartoons
items.description: A short-lived 1990s regional California kids show that was reportedly stopped by Michael Eisner.

items.name: Michael Eisner
items.description: The Disney CEO said to have personally blocked King Koopa's Kool Kartoons.

items.name: Koji Kondo
items.description: The composer of the Super Mario music, who struggled to follow up the first game.

items.name: Abadox
items.description: Next week's NES game.

items.name: Adventures of Lolo 2
items.description: A game in an upcoming episode; the first Lolo is already on the Essential Games List.

items.name: Al Unser Jr.'s Turbo Racing
items.description: Another upcoming NES game, a racing game named for the driver.

links.label: Wikipedia: Al Unser Jr.'s Turbo Racing

items.name: Barker Bill's Trick Shooting
items.description: The Nintendo light-gun game that comes before Dr. Mario.

items.name: Dr. Mario
items.description: The next major Nintendo release the hosts will cover.

items.name: NEStalgia Essential Games List
items.description: The show's list of NES games that define the system; Super Mario Bros. 3 was voted on early in the episode.
